title: Annotatio VI §.VIII: drop contradictory/unrevealed speech and invidious ‘they pretend’ charge
pass_a_gloss: But this one thing remains: that the most distinguished Author, and as many as foster and widen the Protestant Schism, wholly abstain from modes of speaking in the Holy Supper partly unrevealed and at once contradictory (such as: Christ’s body, food though merely Spiritual, yet properly and Orally eaten; and likewise properly and orally eaten by the unworthy; also that proper Eating, of solid food though it be, is yet not dental nor guttural, &c.; moreover that Oral Eating, though done with the body’s natural mouth, is yet merely Supernatural and Heavenly, because the Object of Oral Eating, Christ’s Body, is only supernatural and Heavenly food, nevertheless to be eaten with a natural and earthly Instrument); partly from profane and Christian-Religion-unworthy sayings (such as: presence of Christ’s body by faith is a mere Fiction; Spiritual Eating is merely imaginary; Faith is mere imagination and thought); and finally partly from invidious sayings most gravely wounding Christian charity — such as: THE REFORMED DO NOT BELIEVE WHAT THEY PRETEND TO BELIEVE, THEY THINK ONE THING AND SAY ANOTHER, AND WITH WORDS INSIDIOUSLY CONCEIVED AND COMPOSED TO DECEIVE MEN CONFESS THE PRESENCE OF CHRIST’S BODY IN THE HOLY SUPPER.
pass_b_english: What remains: the Author and all who widen Protestant schism must drop unrevealed, contradictory Supper-speech (spiritual food orally chewed; Indigni oral eating; non-dental solid eating; natural mouth yet merely heavenly, &c.).
Drop also profane charges (faith-presence a fiction; spiritual eating imaginary; faith mere thought) and the invidious claim that the Reformed pretend belief while saying another thing to deceive.
source_text: Sed hoc unum restat, ut Clarissimus Autor, & quotquot Schisma Protestanticum fovent atque dilatant, à modis loquendi in S. Cœna, partim non revelatis, simulque contradictoriis (quales sunt: corpus Christi, cibum merè licèt Spiritualem, propriè tamen & Oraliter manducari; Itemque ab indignis propriè & oraliter manducari; Propriam etiam Manducationem, solidi licèt cibi, non esse tamen dentalem, nec gutturalem, &c.; Oralem insuper Manducationem, ore corporis naturali licèt factam, esse tamen merè Supernaturalem & Cælestem, propterea, quòd Objectum Manducationis Oralis, Corpus Christi, supernaturalis & Cœlestis tantum cibus est, Instrumento nihilominus naturali & terrestri manducandus); Partim à profanis & Religione Christiana indignis (quales sunt: Præsentiam corporis Christi per fidem, esse merum Commentum; Manducationem Spiritualem esse merè imaginariam; Fidem, meram imaginationem & cogitationem); partim denique ab invidiosis & charitatem christianam gravissimè lædentibus, quales sunt: REFORMATOS NON CREDERE, QUOD SE CREDERE SIMULANT, ILLOS ALIUD SENTIRE, ALIUD LOQUI, VERBIS INSIDIOSE CONCEPTIS ET AD DECIPIENDOS HOMINES COMPOSITIS, PRÆSENTIAM CORPORIS CHRISTI IN S. CŒNA FATERI — toti abstineant.

lemmas.latin: REFORMATOS NON CREDERE, QUOD SE CREDERE SIMULANT
lemmas.gloss: THE REFORMED DO NOT BELIEVE WHAT THEY PRETEND

notes: Drop contradictory speech and invidious charge.
